lines.trans: Miss—oh my, we have met before! Do you not know our complex requires head-in parking? I need you to repark that car.
Oh, it slipped my mind—I will park head-first from now on!
From now on? I would like you to repark it right this instant!
Right now I am rushing upstairs just to grab something—as soon as I bring it down, I am pulling the car straight out anyway.
I am doing this for the peace and order of our apartment complex! Do you know how harmful exhaust fumes are to this flowerbed?!
Put yourself in the shoes of those flowerbed plants—imagine how offended they must feel!
You have a point—I sincerely apologize for failing to consider things from the point of view of the plants!
Sorry, young lady, I simply do not trust your word.
Then what—should I write you a signed pledge right here? You care about the feelings of the plants and not a fellow resident?!

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!
Goodbye! (go safely)
Let us do that (go (honorific)) right away.

meanings.en: to have, to possess, to take

examples.trans: I have an interest.
Please bring it (take it and come).

examples.text: 그럼 어떻게 지금 뭐 각서라도 써드려요? 화초의 입장만 생각하시고 제 입장은 생각 안 하세요?
examples.trans: Then what—should I write you a signed pledge right here? You care about the feelings of the plants and not a fellow resident?!
This point about even a written pledge is really important.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

examples.text: 아가씨, 어머 우리 구면이네! 우리 아파트는 전면 주차하는 거 몰라요? 차 좀 다시 세워줘야겠는데.
examples.trans: Miss—oh my, we have met before! Do you not know our complex requires head-in parking? I need you to repark that car.
This point about have met before is really important.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.
Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

examples.text: 내 말이 그 말이다! 걔는 뭐 이렇게 급히 할 말이 있다고 이 비 오는데 말이야!
examples.trans: That is my exact point! What could she possibly need to say so urgently in this pouring rain?!

examples.text: 제가 지금은 집에 뭘 급히 가지러 올라가는 길이었거든요. 그것만 가지고 내려오면 그냥 차를 빼서 가면 돼서요.
examples.trans: Right now I am rushing upstairs just to grab something—as soon as I bring it down, I am pulling the car straight out anyway.

examples.text: 바로 길 건너에 비뇨기과가 새로 열었거든.
examples.trans: A new urology clinic just opened right across the street.
The topic of street, road came up during this shoot.
Oh, it slipped my mind—I will park head-first from now on!
Let us do that (it slipped my mind) right away.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

examples.text: 제가 지금은 집에 뭘 급히 가지러 올라가는 길이었거든요. 그것만 가지고 내려오면 그냥 차를 빼서 가면 돼서요.
examples.trans: Right now I am rushing upstairs just to grab something—as soon as I bring it down, I am pulling the car straight out anyway.
Let us do that (once I come down) right away.

meanings.note: repeating an action or returning to a previous state

examples.trans: Please say that one more time.
I'll come back in a moment.

meanings.en: immediately, on the spot, right this second
meanings.note: often paired with 지금 (지금 당장) for strong emphasis

examples.trans: Try calling right away.
We have to start right this second.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

examples.text: 나는 여기 아파트의 안녕과 질서를 위해서 이러는 거거든! 이 매연이 화단에 얼마나 안 좋다고!
examples.trans: I am doing this for the peace and order of our apartment complex! Do you know how harmful exhaust fumes are to this flowerbed?!

examples.text: 저희 어머니가 재활용 쓰레기, 매연 이런 문제에 워낙 민감하셔서요. 별명이 여의도 오지라퍼라고…
examples.trans: My mother is extra sensitive about recycling and exhaust fumes—her nickname is actually the Yeouido Busybody…

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.en: to be sorry; to feel apologetic
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective; used with peers or younger people (whereas 죄송하다 is honorific/humble).

examples.trans: I'm really sorry I'm late.

examples.text: 미안하지만 다시 한 번 말씀해 주세요.
examples.trans: I'm sorry, but please say that one more time.

examples.text: 그러네요, 제가 미처 화초의 입장에서 생각하지 못한 점 정말 사과드리고요!
examples.trans: You have a point—I sincerely apologize for failing to consider things from the point of view of the plants!
I thought it over again (beforehand).

examples.text: 신디야, 이제 내가 네 엄마야. 엄마만 믿고 따라오면 돼.
examples.trans: Cindy, from now on I am your mother—just trust Mom and follow me.
Let us do that (trusting and) right away.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 네가 회식 가면 본인이 뭐가 되냐고.
examples.trans: She asked what that would make her look like if you showed up at the dinner.
Here the word for 'she herself' is key.

examples.text: 본인이 저 화초들이라고 생각해 봐요, 얼마나 불쾌하겠어!
examples.trans: Put yourself in the shoes of those flowerbed plants—imagine how offended they must feel!
It is really displeased they must feel compared to what I expected.

빼다.gloss: to take out; to remove; to exclude

meanings.en: to take out; to remove; to exclude
meanings.note: Used for removing someone from a schedule or taking something out.

examples.trans: Please take my name off the list.
I took the key out of my pocket.

examples.text: 그러네요, 제가 미처 화초의 입장에서 생각하지 못한 점 정말 사과드리고요!
examples.trans: You have a point—I sincerely apologize for failing to consider things from the point of view of the plants!
Let us do that (offer my apologies) right away.
Good idea.
Come to mind.
Let's I think together today.
I worked hard to I think yesterday too.
Please pull over at the taxi stand over there.
Let us do that (please stop the car) right away.

examples.text: 그럼 어떻게 지금 뭐 각서라도 써드려요? 화초의 입장만 생각하시고 제 입장은 생각 안 하세요?
examples.trans: Then what—should I write you a signed pledge right here? You care about the feelings of the plants and not a fellow resident?!
Let us do that (should I write you) right away.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!
Did you hear about this miss, young lady?
I was busy today because of miss, young lady.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.
Hi! Have you been well?
See you tomorrow, bye!

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)
Go forward.
Do well in the future.

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?
Oh my, so nice to meet you!
Oh my, I left my phone behind.

meanings.en: how much / how many / how long
meanings.note: Asks about degree, amount, price, or duration

examples.trans: How much will the repair cost be?
How long does it take from here to the station?

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

examples.text: 가위바위보에서 졌다고 신디가 짐도 다 들고 올라갔대요.
examples.trans: Because she lost rock-paper-scissors, they say Cindy carried all the bags up herself.
This expression comes from 'they say she went up'.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.
Let's for the sake of together today.
I worked hard to for the sake of yesterday too.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.
Even if I put myself in that female celebrity's shoes…
Here the word for 'even in the position of' is key.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.
Did you hear about this to the forefront?
I was busy today because of to the forefront.

meanings.note: Used when reading decimal numbers, e.g. 오 점 칠 (5.7).

examples.text: 이번 주 시청률은 오 점 칠이에요.
examples.trans: This week's ratings are five point seven.
I learned many good points.

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
